newsitem.title: USA: Comsat settles dispute over board election.
newsitem.headline: Comsat settles dispute over board election.

text.p: Comsat Corp said Tuesday a protential proxy contest in connection with the election of directors at its upcoming annual meeting had been settled.

Under the agreement with Herbert Denton and Guy Wyser-Pratte, Comsat said, four new nominees will stand for election to the board: two selected by the board and two selected by members of the Denton/Wyser-Pratte group.
The remaining eight nominees will be selected by Comsat's board from among the current elected directors.
The annual meeting is scheduled for August 15.
The 12 elected directors stand for election annually. The board also has three directors, appointed by the President of the United States, who serve three-year terms.
Comsat said the board will announce its two new nominees later this month.
The two designees of the Denton/Wyser-Pratte group are Wyser Pratte and Larry Schafran, managing partner of L.G. Schafran and Associates and chairman of the executive committee of Dart Group Corp.
Under the agreement, Comsat will establish a Strategic Planning Committee comprised of three directors, two of whom will be selected by the board. The third will be Schafran.

The agreement also provides that the Denton/Wyser-Pratte Group will be entitled to two nominees at the 1998 annual meeting. The group has agreed to support the agreed-on slate at both meetings, Comsat said.
In connection with the settlement, Comsat said, it is dismissing litigation claims against Denton/Wyser-Pratte Group members.
The company said the group holds about 1.5 million Comsat shares out of 49.1 million outstanding.
